claude.result:
`./game.html` is complete — all 13 systems implemented, no TODOs deferred. Summary:

**Built:** Seeded mulberry32 RNG (no `Math.random` anywhere), 8×8 procedural map with 5 terrains and adjacency bonuses, 9-resource economy with real production chains (ore→metal, ash→soil→food), individual colonists with 4 jobs/skill/fatigue/morale, storage caps with logged overflow, a 12-node research tree, a 12-event deck (5 with genuine tradeoff choices), a caravan with drifting supply/demand pricing, ashstorms with scaling severity and repairable damage, plain-JSON save/load with validation, win/lose conditions with a scored summary screen, a full tabbed UI with custom tooltips and a keyboard interface, and a Dev panel with 23 test assertions plus a 200-turn deterministic benchmark.

**Verification:** This sandbox blocks script execution (Bash commands beyond read-only ones require approval that never arrives here, and no browser/chromium-cli is available), so I couldn't run the Dev panel's own tests or load the page in a live browser as I normally would before calling UI work done. Instead I did a complete manual line-by-line read of the file and cross-checked every `getElementById`/`querySelector` call against the actual DOM — all resolve correctly, no duplicate IDs. That review caught and fixed six real bugs before you'd ever see them:

- Colonist ID counter was a module global, not state-scoped — would have made two benchmark runs from the same seed produce different hashes, failing the determinism requirement.
- Terrain-guarantee logic could let a later guarantee (rock) cannibalize an earlier one (ruins), risking a map with zero ruins tiles.
- The Save/Load panel had no nav button pointing at it — it existed but was permanently unreachable.
- Global Space/1-5 keyboard shortcuts didn't exclude `<select>` elements, so tabbing to a colonist-assignment dropdown and pressing Space would end the turn instead of opening it.
- Migrant-arrival event weight was tuned too low (~3 expected arrivals over 60 turns) to realistically reach the required population-12 win condition — rebalanced so it's achievable with good play but not trivial.
- A stray dead function and one player-facing tooltip with leftover internal notes.

I'd still recommend opening it in an actual browser yourself and clicking "Run Tests" / "Run Benchmark" on the Dev tab before you trust it fully — that's the one step I couldn't complete here.
